reasons: The visible parts handle duplicates and unresolved values, but the promotion and revert steps are not in the packet.
No test for the store logic is shown; the evidence rules test covers only the comparison and date parts used here.

terms.meaning: one stored reading of a project measure, such as a budget or a date, with its source and status
a unique label for where a value came from, used to stop importing the same value twice
a text key for the basis tags on a value, so values on different bases are kept apart
a person checking a value and its source before it is used
insert a row, or update it if it already exists
a group of database changes that all succeed or all fail together

sections.name: File setup, Db, Tx, Exec
sections.title: Store setup and rules at a glance
sections.what: Explains the three main rules: a source is one page and one quote; a project field is mirrored into value points without overwriting; a project field changes only through promotion after vetting.
sections.why: Likely reason: the file's rules are central to trust in the data, so they are stated first.
sections.watch_out: Changing one rule without the others can let silent overwrites back in.

sections.name: SourceInput
sections.title: Shape of a source
sections.what: Describes what is stored for a source: the web address, the quote, and optional details such as publisher, title, date, quality tier, anchors and origin.
sections.why: Likely reason: each source needs enough detail to be trusted and found again.
sections.watch_out: Fields are optional, so a source can be saved with little detail.

sections.name: upsertSource
sections.title: Saving a source without overwriting
sections.what: Finds or creates a source by its normalised address and quote hash. When it already exists, it only fills in details that are still empty, so an earlier import is never replaced.
sections.why: Likely reason: earlier imports may hold corrected details that a later import should not undo.
sections.watch_out: A blank field can be filled later by any import, so the first non-empty value is kept permanently.

sections.name: linkValueSource
sections.title: Attaching a source to a value
sections.what: Links a value point to a source with its rank, role (primary, corroborating or alternative), mapping and extraction details. A repeat link does nothing.
sections.why: Likely reason: one value can have several supporting sources, and each link must be stored once.
sections.watch_out: The mapping text records how the value was read from the source, so it should be kept in step with the rules.

sections.name: valueFingerprint, Comparable
sections.title: Fingerprint of a value
sections.what: Creates a text fingerprint of what a value says: its resolved date, its rounded number and unit, or its text. It ignores where the value came from.
sections.why: Likely reason: two values that say the same thing from different sources should have the same fingerprint.
sections.watch_out: Numbers are rounded to three decimal places, so very small differences are treated as equal in the fingerprint.

sections.name: statedStep
sections.title: Rounding step of a stated figure
sections.what: Works out the rounding step a figure was stated to, from its text when the text carries the number, or else from its stored number. It is ignored if the text does not scale to the stored value.
sections.why: Likely reason: 1.3 billion and 1,231.7 million are only the same to the precision the source states, so the step is needed.
sections.watch_out: Figures stated with no decimals are treated as exact to the last digit when the text is not used.

sections.name: sameValue
sections.title: Checking whether two readings agree
sections.what: Decides whether two readings say the same thing. Dates must match exactly. Figures must share a unit and lie within half the coarser rounding step. Basis is not compared here, because values on different bases are kept apart earlier.
sections.why: Likely reason: sources round figures differently, so exact matching would flag false conflicts.
sections.watch_out: Figures with no unit match only when their numbers agree, so a missing unit can hide a real difference.

sections.name: describeValue
sections.title: Describing a value for people
sections.what: Makes a short readable description of a value, showing the stated date with its resolved date, a number with its unit, or the text.
sections.why: Likely reason: conflict notes and the viewer need one readable form of each value.
sections.watch_out: An unresolved date shows the word unresolved, so a reader must notice that.

sections.name: addValuePoint, ProjectRow
sections.title: Adding a value without overwriting
sections.what: Adds a value point without overwriting anything. A repeat import does nothing; a value matching the current one attaches to it; a first value becomes current; an unresolved value is kept for vetting but never used; a different value is kept beside the current one with a conflict note.
sections.why: Likely reason: nothing may change silently, so every new reading is stored for a person to decide.
sections.watch_out: Only the same basis is compared, so a value on a different basis is stored as a separate current value.

sections.name: dateAssumption
sections.title: Reading an approved assumption on a date
sections.what: Looks in the project's saved date assumptions for a note of the form approximate with a stated date and a rule, and returns that stated text and rule for the matching measure.
sections.why: Likely reason: some dates were approximated earlier and the project records how.
sections.watch_out: The note must match an exact text pattern, so a differently worded note is not found.

sections.name: promotedMirror
sections.title: Reading which value a project column mirrors
sections.what: Returns the id of the value point that a project column was last set from, as recorded when it was promoted.
sections.why: Likely reason: the system needs to know which value is behind each project field.
sections.watch_out: Missing records return nothing, so a field with no record looks as if it was never promoted.

sections.name: yardBudgetBasisTags
sections.title: Basis tags of a budget
sections.what: Returns the basis tags stated in a project's budget text, using the same reading rules as the metrics file.
sections.why: Likely reason: the Yard's budget text is the usual source of a budget's basis.
sections.watch_out: Only the budget text is read, so a basis stated elsewhere is not picked up.

sections.name: columnValue, SyncReport
sections.title: Turning a project field into a value point
sections.what: Takes one yard project field (money, capacity, or a date) and turns it into a stored value record that notes its unit, its stated date wording, and any basis tags from the budget text. It also defines the report shape that counts created, matched, and conflicting values.
sections.why: Likely reason: a stored value needs to carry where it came from and in what unit, so it can be compared and checked later.
sections.watch_out: Money is stored in US$M, and a capacity of zero is treated as 'not reported' and replaced with the project's own MW value.

sections.name: syncValuePointsFromProject
sections.title: Copying one project's values and quotes
sections.what: For one project, copies its benchmark fields into value points, links each to its quoted source text, and returns counts of what was created, matched, or conflicted.
sections.why: The code comment says it is idempotent, meaning running it again should not create duplicates.
sections.watch_out: A value that a promotion has set is kept only while it still matches. If the project field changes, a new value point is created and may be marked as a conflict.

sections.name: PromotionRefused, fmtField
sections.title: Refusal error and text formatter
sections.what: Defines a special error type used when a promotion is refused for a stated reason, and a small helper that turns a field value into plain text for the change log.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. A separate error type lets callers tell a deliberate refusal from an unexpected crash.
sections.watch_out: Code that checks for refusals depends on this exact error type name.

sections.name: promoteVettedValue (part 1)
sections.title: Making a vetted value current
sections.what: Makes a vetted value the current one for its project, metric, and basis. If asked, it also writes the value into the project field. Every change is logged with what it replaced. It refuses unless the latest vetting record says vetted.
sections.why: The code comment says every promotion is logged so it can be reverted later.
sections.watch_out: Money promotions are refused when the value has no US$ amount, so a value that only has a local-currency figure cannot be written to a money field.

sections.name: promoteVettedValue (part 2)
sections.title: Continuation of the promotion function
sections.what: This part has no code of its own. The promotion function continues in the section before it and closes there.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It appears to be a split point in the file.

sections.name: revertPromotion
sections.title: Undoing a promotion
sections.what: Reverses one logged promotion. It restores the old field value only if nothing has changed the field since, and makes the previously current value current again. The original log entry is kept and marked as reverted, and a new log entry records the revert with a note.
sections.why: The code comment says the original record is kept and a new one is added, so the history stays complete.
sections.watch_out: The revert is refused if the field has changed since the promotion, or if a later promotion now owns that field. The user must give a written reason, or the revert is refused.

sections.name: openPromotions
sections.title: Listing promotions not yet undone
sections.what: Returns the promotions of one value that have not been reverted, newest first, so a person can see what could still be undone.
sections.why: Likely reason: it supports the revert step by showing which promotions are still open.
sections.watch_out: It finds promotions by matching text in the change log source. Changing that wording breaks the search.

sections.name: METRICS_BY_COLUMN
sections.title: Finding a metric by its field name
sections.what: Looks up the metric definition whose project field name matches a given column name. Revert uses it to know whether a field holds money, capacity, or a date.
sections.why: Likely reason: a revert must restore the field in the right form, and the metric kind decides that.
sections.watch_out: It returns nothing when no metric matches, so any caller must handle a missing result.

summary: Stores sources and value points, compares values, and keeps project fields in step with them without overwriting anything silently.
purpose: Keeps the evidence record of every project value honest: each value has a source, each change is recorded for vetting, and project fields change only after review.
why: Likely reason: the review process depends on nothing being overwritten silently, so new readings are added beside the current one for vetting.
how: It finds or creates a source by its address and quote, attaches sources to value points, and compares new readings with the current one using rounding rules. A new reading that matches the current one is not stored again. A different reading is stored beside the current value for vetting, and an unresolved reading is kept but never used. Project fields are mirrored into value points, and a field changes only through promoteVettedValue after vetting.
inputs: Source details, value readings with their basis and dates, project rows and their attributes, and reviewer decisions.
outputs: Stored sources, value points and links, and outcome labels such as same as current, inserted as current, inserted as conflict, or already imported.
risks: Several rules depend on exact stored values and text, so a schema change can break them. Only part of the file is visible in the packet, so the promotion and revert steps cannot be fully checked here.
debug: If a value is missing, check its origin key, which blocks a second import of the same value. If a value is wrongly flagged as a conflict, check sameValue and the basis key. If a project field did not change, check that the value has a passing vetting record.
